$schema_note: canary.local device registry — one entry per device flavor. The page renders a pairing card per entry; entries with an `emulator` block get the live wasm firmware on their glass. `fw_train` names the release train this registry snapshot teaches; per-version emulator artifacts are named dist/<id>@<version>.js when built from a release tag (see canary-local/README.md §Versioning).

devices.name: Canary Fence Guard
devices.tagline: Meshtastic on the property line — the fence becomes a witness. Coming soon.

network.mdns: none — the fence line is past the WiFi by definition
network.mqtt: via mesh gateway (concept): fence-event claims + signed chain

concept.idea: A perimeter witness clamped to the chain-link at the property's edge — past the WiFi, past mains power. It would feel the fence's own vibration signature (climb, cut, rattle), debounce it into the same small signed claims every Canary speaks, and carry them home over the Meshtastic LoRa mesh, solar-fed, with the relay pod as its first hop.

points.v: clamped to chain-link in a shaded run — panel in the sun, cell in the shade; lithium ages in heat and must not charge below freezing.
Ed25519-signed fence-event claims over the mesh, hash-chained — and Meshtastic's position broadcast stays off: a perimeter node must not map the perimeter.
solar over battery via an external charge controller (the kit's onboard charger is a slow ~50-100 mA and has no solar input); target is multi-day overcast survival.
the kit ships with no IP rating — the sealed clamp enclosure, with the antenna stood off the fence's metal plane, is ours to design and print-validate.

radio.v: Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 + Wio-SX1262 (SKU 102010611, $9.90) — same XIAO family as every Canary host; Meshtastic pre-flashed since Oct 2024
Semtech SX1262 · 862-930 MHz, one hardware for EU868/US915 (region set in firmware) · up to +22 dBm · U.FL antenna
ESP32-S3R8 dual-core 240 MHz · 8 MB flash + 8 MB PSRAM · WiFi b/g/n + BLE 5.0 · 21 x 17.8 mm
mainline target seeed-xiao-s3 (HW_MODEL 81), community-supported tier, web-flasher entry 'Seeed XIAO S3'
LIS3DH accelerometer natively supported on the free I2C bus; the Detection Sensor module reads a vibration switch on a free GPIO - a zero-custom-code Phase 0 exists
~130 mA measured as an always-on node (community, single-source) vs ~11.7 mA idle on the nRF52840 sibling kit - an ~11x gap the field mule must adjudicate
2-5 km typical; >2.5 km measured by Seeed on the 2 dBi antenna (open-terrain 20 km+ claims are marketing)

plan: Phase 0, zero custom firmware: stock Meshtastic + LIS3DH on I2C + a vibration switch on a free GPIO (Detection Sensor module) — a field mule on a real fence, measuring false alarms and the solar budget through weather.
Let the mule's power data adjudicate ESP32-S3 vs the nRF52840 sibling kit (~11x idle gap; the S3 buys WiFi and price, the nRF52 buys the battery).
Close the platform question: Meshtastic module on stock firmware vs the native witness stack with a mesh transport.
Then the witness surface: v1 fence canonical, Ed25519 chain, health claims — the same trust rules as the rest of the fleet, position broadcast off forever.
Enclosure last, informed by the mule: chain-link clamp, antenna stood off the metal plane, IP-rated, printed and validated like every other Canary shell.

devices.name: Canary Vision Pro
devices.tagline: The flagship eye — starlight imaging and on-chip sound classification, still speaking only in claims. Coming soon.
devices.board: Seeed reCamera Pro 2GB (Rockchip RV1126B, 3 TOPS NPU)

network.mdns: none — an external adapter source, not a flashed Canary host (concept)
network.web: vendor Web UI + flow editor (device-native; no Canary firmware runs on it)
network.mqtt: none directly — reaches the fleet via the webhook sensor adapter (concept): coarse claims + signed chain

devices.status: coming soon — concept, config-only integration designed, no bench unit yet

concept.idea: Canary Vision Pro asks a different question than the rest of the fleet: not 'can we afford a sensor here,' but 'what does the one chokepoint that actually matters deserve.' It runs its own on-chip NPU — vision and sound classification entirely local, no cloud, no pixels leaving the box — and reaches the fleet the same way Frigate or an ESPHome radar kit does: through the sensor adapter contract, not new firmware. Point its flow editor's HTTP action at the webhook adapter, and a $300 starlight camera becomes one more small, signed claim in the log — same discipline as a $10 sensor, sharper eyes.

points.v: the 8 MP SC850SL starlight sensor resolves real detail after dark, where PIR/RF sensors can only say 'something moved'; on-device sound classification adds glass-break/alarm coverage no cheap sensor in the fleet offers.

a classifier label and confidence score, and nothing else — the sensor adapter contract's Claim type has no field a free-text caption could occupy. The chip can run a VLM/LLM and describe a scene in words; that path is deliberately never wired to the webhook route.

points.k: How it would join the fleet
points.v: zero new firmware. Its flow editor's HTTP action node POSTs to the existing webhook adapter (src/adapter/webhook.rs) — the same config-only pattern already proven for the MR60BHA2 kit's ESPHome bridge.

the module ships with native CAN, GPIO, UART and PoE unused by this integration today — it pairs naturally with the 4.3B dev-playground's RS485/Modbus/CAN industrial story on a site that already runs that wiring.

radio.v: Rockchip RV1126B — quad-core Arm Cortex-A53, 3 TOPS NPU (Rockchip RV1126B datasheet)
8 MP SC850SL starlight sensor, 4K30 fps (Seeed reCamera hardware wiki)
2 GB RAM / 16 GB eMMC on this SKU (Seeed product page)
Gigabit Ethernet, 2.4G/5G WiFi, Bluetooth 5.4, USB-C 3.0, PoE (Seeed reCamera hardware wiki)
CAN, GPIO, UART, MIPI-DSI onboard — present on the module, unused by this integration today (Seeed reCamera hardware wiki)
dual onboard microphones — the sound-classification path this concept routes (Seeed reCamera hardware wiki)
vendor firmware supports CV, VLM, LLM, STT and TTS locally; Canary Vision Pro's route uses classification labels only (CNX Software coverage)

plan: Bench: confirm the flow editor's HTTP action node actually produces the documented {"confidence": ...} payload shape against a real webhook listener.
Bench: pin a SenseCraft audio-classification model for glass-break / alarm / raised-voice and confirm its class labels match the ClaimKind mapping in docs/hardware/canary_vision_pro_recamera.md.
Verify bearer/HMAC auth and TLS survive a device restart before calling this off-loopback-ready.

Print-fit canary_vision_pro_mount.scad (bridges reCamera's magnetic/1/4"-20 mount onto the shared stud interface) against a real unit once one is on the bench — the mesh renders clean today but has never touched actual hardware.
Promote from 'concept' to 'released' only after a real unit's claims round-trip into the sealed log — the same bar as every other Canary.

devices.name: Canary Car Mode
devices.tagline: A stock mesh node in your car's USB port — no firmware, no wiring, no circuit to rot. Coming soon.
devices.board: Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 + Wio-SX1262 (Meshtastic, pre-flashed, stock)
senses: vehicle power-on/off, via a stock Meshtastic Detection Sensor Module (concept)

network.mdns: none — a stock Meshtastic node, not a flashed Canary host (concept)
network.web: none — no onboard config surface beyond stock Meshtastic's own app/CLI
network.mqtt: via the meshtastic gateway + adapter (concept): coarse vehicle_arrival_departure claims + signed chain

devices.status: coming soon — concept, config-only design, no bench unit yet

concept.idea: Canary Car Mode is the zero-build answer to 'tell the fleet when I arrive or leave': a completely stock Meshtastic node, powered directly from the car's ignition-switched USB port, with nothing wired to it at all. The node's own power state IS the ignition signal — no CAN bus, no custom firmware, no custom circuit. Its Detection Sensor Module GPIO is left floating with an internal pull-up, so 'the chip has power' reads as 'triggered' for free. Arrival is a detection packet on boot; departure is never an explicit packet (a real Meshtastic firmware bug makes that unreliable) — it's inferred the same way every other presence source in this fleet already works: silence past a timeout means gone.

points.k: Why no firmware and no circuit
points.v: the node's power supply already is the signal — it can only run while the car provides it. Stock Meshtastic firmware gets upstream's own maintenance forever; there is no bespoke sketch to rot.

points.k: Why departure is inferred, not announced
points.v: a documented Meshtastic firmware bug (github.com/meshtastic/firmware#8977) means the Detection Sensor Module's OFF transition can't be trusted. Rather than build a last-gasp/supercap workaround around someone else's open bug, departure is read from the ABSENCE of periodic heartbeats — the same pattern this fleet's presence claims already use everywhere else.
the car's USB port must actually be ignition/ACC-switched, not always-hot for phone charging — check this on the bench before trusting the design at all.

points.k: Shares its research, doesn't duplicate it
points.v: same $9.90 kit already researched for Canary Fence Guard, same Meshtastic mechanics documented once in docs/meshtastic_integration.md — this card and its doc only add what's specific to reading a car's power state.

radio.v: Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 + Wio-SX1262 (SKU 102010611, $9.90) — Meshtastic pre-flashed since Oct 2024, same kit as Canary Fence Guard
USB-powered directly from the vehicle's ignition-switched port — no battery, nothing to charge or maintain
Detection Sensor Module (Meshtastic firmware >= 2.2.2), GPIO left floating with use_pullup=true — reads triggered the instant the chip has power, no external components
inferred from heartbeat silence (state_broadcast_interval), not an explicit OFF packet — see the known firmware bug below
Detection Sensor Module OFF-transition reliability bug, tracked upstream — the whole reason this design avoids depending on a transition packet at all

sources.name: Seeed Fence Guard kit research (same hardware)
meshtastic/firmware issue #8977 — Detection Sensor OFF-transition bug

plan: Bench: confirm a floating, pulled-high GPIO actually fires a boot-time detection alert the way a real switch closing would — this is a repurposing of the module, not its documented use case.
Bench: pin the Meshtastic firmware version tested and confirm whether issue #8977 affects it before trusting anything about OFF transitions, even indirectly.
Bench: measure real heartbeat timing to size a sane Home Assistant availability timeout (the current design guesses ~2x state_broadcast_interval).
Verify the target vehicle's USB port is genuinely ignition-switched, not always-hot — per-vehicle, not assumable.
Scope and build the optional stale-node watchdog (sealed-log ObjectRemovedFromZone on silence) if a witnessed departure event — not just an HA-inferred one — turns out to matter.
concept.plan_intro: No firmware stub either — stock Meshtastic needs none. What's left is bench validation of a repurposed module behavior, not new code.

persona.name: Rally the Homecoming Scout
persona.shape: a compact canary shaped like a USB stick, key-shaped tail feathers, and a small radio-mast crest
persona.story: Rally doesn't carry a single wire of its own — it just rides along in the one plug that only comes alive when you do. Rally never asks the car anything, never listens to its bus, never learns where it's been. It just says 'I'm awake' the moment you are, and goes quiet, honestly, the moment you're not.

Households already running (or willing to run) a Meshtastic gateway
The most maintenance-free vehicle sensor in the fleet, by construction
persona.catchphrase: I only ever say I'm here — and I mean it because I couldn't lie if I tried.

persona.name: Hush the Wire Listener
persona.shape: a low, alert canary with a single coiled antenna-whisker and folded, listening-only wings — no beak wide enough to speak
persona.story: Hush was built with no voice on purpose. It rides quietly on your car's own wire, hears the ignition switch the way every other module in the car already does, and says only ever one thing outward: here, or gone. Hush never asks the car a question, never sends it a command, and never once remembers where the car has been — only whether it's home.
good_for: Telling the household fleet when a car arrives or leaves, without a phone geofence
Households with a small always-on Linux hub (a Pi) willing to ride along in the vehicle
Proving, structurally, that a witness can listen to a car without ever tracking it
persona.catchphrase: I only ever answer one question: are you home?
